name: Thekua (Khajuria)
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated coconut or dessicated coconut
Ghee or oil for deep frying
instructions: 1. Dissolve the jaggery in a little warm water to make a thick syrup.
2. In a large bowl, mix wheat flour, grated coconut, cardamom powder, and fennel seeds.
3. Add melted ghee to the flour mixture and rub with your fingers until the texture resembles breadcrumbs.
4. Gradually add the jaggery syrup to form a very tight, semi-stiff dough.
5. Divide the dough into small lemon-sized balls and press them onto a patterned mold (sancha) or a textured surface to get a flattened shape.
6. Heat ghee in a deep pan and fry the thekuas on low-to-medium heat until they turn golden brown and crispy.
7. Remove and let them cool completely to achieve their signature crunch.
description: Thekua is a quintessential sweet snack from Bihar and Jharkhand, most famously associated with the Chhath Puja festival. It serves as a sacred 'prasad' offered to the Sun God, prized for its long shelf life, rustic texture, and distinct flavor profile derived from jaggery and coconut.
